key_insight: Accurate tumor-growth predictions can still come from the wrong underlying law, so symbolic discovery must be judged by mathematical validity and law recovery—not fit alone.
engineering_relevance: For data-driven modeling in biology and other sparse-data systems, the workflow highlights that coefficient refitting, candidate filtering, and ranking should be designed to avoid selecting plausible but incorrect governing equations.
method: Symbolic regression proposes candidate growth laws from sparse noisy tumor data
Mathematical admissibility checks and coefficient refitting refine retained models
LLM-based ranking is compared against training-error selection and classical nonlinear least squares
evidence_signal: On synthetic Gompertz data, dense noiseless sampling recovered the true family, while sparse noisy sampling often produced alternative laws; nonlinear least squares usually reduced law error, whereas PINN refitting often increased it.
watch_item: LLM rankings and good trajectory fits can mask mathematical errors, so implementation should include explicit law-recovery and admissibility evaluation before accepting a model.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
